RETIRED 2026-09-18 on Jeff's ruling. This asserted a signed runtime-approval receipt that the CRM launcher required before starting: nine pinned keys, a runtime fingerprint, and a hash of the launcher against both the running copy and its source. The receipt was never created, so the strict launcher could never start the service, and on 2026-08-26 a weaker script was installed into ~/.local/bin and run instead. The design was abandoned in practice six weeks before it was abandoned on paper. harajlim/outbound_with_jeff_and_marv#624 makes the installed launcher the versioned one and turns its clean-checkout refusal on by default, so there is no receipt left to check. What still matters, that the installed launcher matches its source, is crm-launcher-install, which is a separate live check and is the one that caught this.

Rewritten 2026-09-18 for the launcher that shipped in harajlim/outbound_with_jeff_and_marv#624. The four receipt strings this used to require are gone with the receipt design. The three refusals below survive because they are the ones that ever ran. The clean-checkout default is required in its exact form: the bypassed launcher carried CRM_RUNTIME_REQUIRE_CLEAN:-0, so the gate read as present in the source while being off in production, and forbidding that spelling is what stops it returning.
